blocks.text: SESSION 1 — Concept · Key Points · Memory Technique. Read, absorb, stop.
1. Concept Explained Simply

The Preliminary Phase happens before the first ADM cycle begins. It sets up the organisation's ability to do architecture work properly, consistently, and with authority. It answers five fundamental questions: Where do we do architecture? (scope) · What do we do it with? (framework) · Why do we do it? (drivers) · Who does it? (team/governance) · How do we do it? (process/tools/principles).
2. Key Points
Two objectives:

items: **Determine** the Architecture Capability desired (review context, scope elements, identify existing frameworks, establish maturity target)
**Establish** the Architecture Capability (define Organisational Model for EA, define Architecture Governance, select tools, define Architecture Principles)

blocks.text: Six steps — "Scope, Governance, Team, Principles, Tailor, Tools"
Three types of tailoring — **TPC**: Terminology · Process · Content
Three enterprise scope categories: **Core** (most affected, most value) · **Soft** (will see change, not directly targeted) · **Extended** (outside scope but affected)
Key outputs: Organisational Model for EA · Tailored Architecture Framework (including Architecture Principles) · Initial Architecture Repository · Architecture Governance Framework
3. Memory Technique
"Where What Why Who How" · "Scope, Governance, Team, Principles, Tailor, Tools" · TPC = "The Proper Customisation"
EXAM TRAP 1 — PRELIMINARY IS NOT PART OF THE ADM CYCLE. It sits outside and before the cycle. Phase A (Architecture Vision) is where the cycle begins. It is not "Phase 0."
EXAM TRAP 2 — PRINCIPLES CREATED IN PRELIMINARY, NOT PHASE A. Architecture Principles are established in the Preliminary Phase. Phase A confirms and elaborates them — it does not create them.
✋ PAUSE POINT — CHECK BEFORE CONTINUING. Answer from memory before reading Session 2.
1. What are the five questions the Preliminary Phase answers?
Where do we do architecture? (scope) · What do we do it with? (framework) · Why do we do it? (drivers) · Who does it? (team/governance) · How do we do it? (process/tools/principles)
2. Name the three types of tailoring in the Preliminary Phase.
Terminology tailoring (language/glossary) · Process tailoring (adapt steps, add checkpoints, link to other processes) · Content tailoring (adapt the Architecture Content Framework).
3. Where are Architecture Principles established — in Preliminary or Phase A?
In the Preliminary Phase. Phase A confirms and elaborates them but does not create them from scratch (unless Preliminary was skipped).
SESSION 2 — Real-World Example · Practice Questions · Part 2 Scenario
4. Real-World Example — GlobalTech Dynamics 365

items: **Scope**: Finance, HR, IT Operations = core. Procurement, Legal = soft. External partners = extended.
**Governance**: Architecture Board reports into IT Steering Committee. Architecture Review checkpoints at every PMO stage gate.
**EA Team**: One Senior EA, two Solution Architects, one Architecture Analyst. Level 1 maturity → target Level 3 within 18 months.

**Principles**: Six established — "Technology follows business strategy"; "Data is a corporate asset"; "All integrations must use approved middleware"; "Cloud-first"; "Reuse before buy, buy before build"; "Security and privacy by design."

**Tailoring**: Terminology tailored for business stakeholders. Architecture Reviews embedded in PMO stage gates. Azure Well-Architected Framework adopted alongside TOGAF's Technology Architecture framework.
**Tools**: Sparx Enterprise Architect · Confluence · JIRA · Power BI.

blocks.text: 5. Part 1 Practice Questions
Q1. Which best describes the primary purpose of the Preliminary Phase?

items: A) To develop the Architecture Vision
B) To prepare the organisation by establishing Architecture Capability, governance, principles, and a tailored framework ✓
C) To review existing architectures and identify gaps
D) To obtain formal sponsorship and budget approval

blocks.text: Answer: B — Preliminary is about setting up the EA capability before any cycle begins.
Q2. An organisation removes redundant ADM steps, adds governance checkpoints, and aligns the ADM to their procurement process. Which type of tailoring?

items: A) Content
B) Terminology
C) Process ✓
D) Framework

blocks.text: Answer: C — removing tasks, adding checkpoints, aligning to other processes = Process tailoring.
Q3. Which is a key output of the Preliminary Phase?

items: A) The Architecture Vision document
B) The Statement of Architecture Work
C) The Tailored Architecture Framework, including Architecture Principles ✓
D) The Architecture Definition Document

blocks.text: Answer: C — the Tailored Architecture Framework (including Architecture Principles) is the primary output.
6. Part 2 Scenario Question (Exam-Authentic Format)

SCENARIO: GlobalTech's CTO directs the newly appointed EA to begin work immediately on the Dynamics 365 migration: "We've wasted too much time in planning already. Go straight to defining the architecture. We'll sort out governance and principles as we go."

rows: Comply. ADM is flexible; Preliminary can run in parallel with Phase A. Acknowledges flexibility correctly but misses the core risk: making architecture decisions before governance rules are established.
Decline until full Preliminary Phase is completed. Contradicts TOGAF — the Standard does not require Preliminary to be fully completed before Phase A begins.

Negotiate a time-boxed, lightweight Preliminary Phase — minimum viable outputs: agree scope, establish a basic governance checkpoint, define a starter set of Architecture Principles, do minimal tailoring. Document the risk and get the CTO's acknowledgement. Best answer.

Begin Phase A immediately and raise absence of Principles and governance as risks in the Architecture Vision, planning to retrospectively establish Preliminary outputs. Better than ignoring the problem but architecturally backwards — decisions made before the rules that govern them exist.
